title: SR-26 Notice Terms for Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) Certificates
content:
An SR-26 is the notice Cardinal Point transmits to a state that coverage certified by a Financial Responsibility Filings (SR-22 / FR-44) certificate has ended. The terms below are the same for all six certificates.

### Occasions for an SR-26

An SR-26 is transmitted on any of these occasions:

- the backing term is cancelled;
- the backing term expires without renewal;
- the requirement is completed and the certificate is released;
- the filer is excluded from, or removed from, the backing term.

The reason recorded on the SR-26 is one of: policy cancelled; policy expired, not renewed; requirement completed; filer excluded or removed.

### Timing and run-off

| Term | All six certificates |
|---|---|
| Latest transmission | within 3 calendar days after the triggering date |
| Earliest transmission | never before the triggering date itself |
| Run-off after the SR-26 | the certificate stops certifying coverage with the state 10 calendar days after the SR-26 transmission date |

**Scope of the transmission window.** For an SR-26 sent because the backing term was cancelled, the window and its starting date are the ones the company fixes for that SR-26. This covers a term that has stayed cancelled and a term that has since been reinstated with a lapse. Every other SR-26 for an ended backing term is transmitted no later than 3 calendar days after the date coverage under the backing term ended.

**Earliest transmission for a lapse.** For a backing term reinstated with a lapse, the date coverage under the term ended is its lapse start date.

**Scope of the run-off.** For an SR-26 sent because the backing term was cancelled, the certificate end date is the SR-26 date plus the run-off days the company fixes for that SR-26. This again covers a term that has stayed cancelled and a term that has since been reinstated with a lapse. Every other SR-26 keeps the certificate end date at the SR-26 date plus 10 calendar days.

### Reinstatement of the backing term

| Situation | All six certificates |
|---|---|
| Backing term reinstated after its SR-26 was transmitted | the certificate is not revived; a new filing is needed |
| Backing term reinstated, or its notice of cancellation rescinded, before the SR-26 would be transmitted | no SR-26 is sent |

**Scope of the second row.** When a backing term, an Owner Auto Policy term or a Named Non-Owner term, was cancelled and has since been reinstated with a lapse, and only then, the SR-26 is still transmitted for the lapse and the certificate does not continue; a backing term reinstated without a lapse, and any backing term whose notice of cancellation was rescinded, before the SR-26 is transmitted still receive no SR-26 and their certificates continue.

### Hypothetical reading

A backing term expires without renewal, and that expiration date is day 0. The SR-26 may go no earlier than day 0 and no later than day 3. If it is transmitted on day 2, the certificate end date is day 12.
